headline: Figma's Agentic Era Just Landed
subheadline: Figma's May release notes are huge — agents, MCP workflows, and write-to-canvas are now official. Plus Brad Frost on designing systems for autonomous agents, and a Cursor security update you should know about.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma May 2026 Release: Agents, MCP Skills, and Write-to-Canvas
sections.description: This is the big one. Figma's May release formally introduces agents, MCP integration, and skills — with write-to-canvas workflows demoed live. Given you're literally building a Figma MCP + Claude integration for your company's white-label sport apps design system, this is required reading. The article walks through three agentic workflows from the livestream, starting from your exact world of MCP and design systems.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Figma May Release Notes Livestream — Co-designing with AI Agents
sections.description: The companion livestream to the release notes above. Live demos from product teams showing real co-design workflows with AI agents — including how to riff on designs with agents and use MCP in practice. Worth watching after you've read the release notes to see the workflows in motion.

sections.label: Listen
sections.title: Agentic Design Systems in 2026 with Brad Frost
sections.description: Brad Frost on how autonomous agents are now assembling UIs using the same components your human designers use. This is directly relevant to your design system work — if agents are consumers of your component library alongside humans, your token architecture and component API decisions take on a whole new dimension. Perfect stroller walk listen. 🍼

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma AI in 2026: Everything It Can Do — and What It Still Can't
sections.description: A clear-eyed overview of where Figma's AI capabilities actually stand — content generation, image editing, smart search, UI drafting, code handoff, and full-site creation. Useful as a mental map of what's real vs. hype, especially as you think about where your MCP integration adds value that Figma's native AI doesn't cover yet.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Cursor SDK — Build Custom Agents for Your Team
sections.description: Cursor just shipped the Cursor SDK in public beta — it lets teams build and deploy custom agents within Cursor. Also new: a Security Review feature with always-on vulnerability scanning for PRs. Since you're vibe-coding in Cursor daily, the SDK could let you create team-specific agents that understand your design system's codebase. Update to v2.5+ for security patches.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Agentic UX — Designing for Users Who Aren't Human
sections.description: Agentic UX is the emerging design discipline of creating interfaces, components, and systems that autonomous AI agents can navigate and use — not just humans. Generative UI (interfaces that assemble themselves in real-time) is part of this. As someone building design systems that will increasingly be consumed by agents, this framing shifts how you think about component APIs, naming, and documentation.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Automating Design Systems with AI: Tokens, Governance, and Agent Workflows
sections.description: A practical guide on using AI agents for design system governance — automating token management, consistency checks, and repetitive system maintenance. Directly maps to your world of Figma tokens and variables. Worth skimming for ideas on what parts of your white-label system could benefit from automated governance.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If agents are now first-class consumers of your design system, what changes?
sections.description: Brad Frost and Figma are both saying the same thing this week: AI agents will assemble UIs from your components. Your naming conventions, token structure, component documentation, and variant logic aren't just for junior designers anymore — they're an API for machines. Does your current design system architecture hold up when the 'user' is Claude, not a human? What would you change?
